enthalpy_units: kJ per mol of atoms; multiplied by 1000 in the equation

pure_ti.note: Same provisional transcription as existing Fig. 7b; 1873 K is below the equilibrium melting point of Ti.

pure_al.note: Critically evaluated experimental reference correlation, not an arithmetic average. Its 14% uncertainty is not validated at 1873 K.

interpolation: Piecewise-linear interpolation of mixing enthalpy, then evaluate KRP; endpoints constrained to zero; no fit to viscosity.

experiment.note: Calorimetry reproduced in Witusiewicz2008 Fig. 7; provisional digitization. Assumed unchanged from 2000 to 1873 K.

pbe.note: Archived 1873 K MD; total energy plus external-pressure pV, pure-liquid references at the same T and model.

scan.note: Archived 1873 K MD; total energy plus external-pressure pV, pure-liquid references at the same T and model.

pbe.note: Same original model, 2000 K versus 1873 K archived MD; not an uncertainty bound for experiment.

scan.note: Same original model, 2000 K versus 1873 K archived MD; not an uncertainty bound for experiment.

limitation_notes: Provisional manual raster digitization; reading tolerance about 0.2 kJ/mol, not experimental uncertainty; original experiments unavailable.
Only experimental enthalpy is transferred from 2000 to 1873 K; both MD enthalpies are evaluated at 1873 K.
PBE input is the 5k model used in Fig. 7a, not the PBE 15k / 2000 K data used in Fig. 6.
Conditional enthalpy SEM is exported at nodes, but no total confidence band is claimed for KRP.
Pure-component viscosity inputs are identical for all three KRP curves.

literature.citation: L. Ya. Kozlov, L. M. Romanov, N. N. Petrov, Prediction of multicomponent metallic melt viscosity, Izv. Vuz. Chern. Metallurg. 3, 7-11 (1983).
